units.translation: in the surging places of Aulis.
for every place of the land is pastured.
in the places of the Libyan land.
not to cross the boundary of places.
to the places below and under the earth.
in the grassy places of my ancient mother.
lathe, tool for turning or boring
lathe, tool for turning or boring
holding in his hands the shuttle, the work of the lathe.
for a piercing sound will come, in harmony with the rays.
the stranger seems to need a clear interpreter.
why did you utter this word so very piercing?
for a piercing, bristling fear cried out from within a nocturnal shriek.
the word is short and clear.
but give me a clear proof.
I will tell you everything clearly.
to know clearly beforehand the remaining pain.
there is need of a long speech to explain these things clearly.
do you know how to indicate clearly?
I will indicate clearly to Agamemnon's wife.
no one knows, so as to report clearly.
by the report which the strangers announced clearly.
it is fitting for a herald to report each thing clearly.
for so great will be the blood-dripping offering.
will you do this so that I have so much strength?
we would not appear to have done so many evils.
if he had received so many wounds.
so great a multitude of woes did he draw upon himself,
so much as this man was under Ilium.
this man, having filled a bowl of so many evils in the house.
for which of men did they admire so much—?

Thus from the copy for τοσοῦτ᾽ ἀριθμόν [so great a number]. Imitating Aeschylus, Tzetzes in his Exegesis on the Iliad p. 92, 8 said τοσουταρίθμου στρατοῦ [of so numerous an army]. Eustathius and Nicetas Choniates said τοσαυτάριθμοι [so numerous], examples of which see in the Thesaurus.
so numerous a multitude of men.
unless τοσοῦτον [so great] should be written in both places.
I am content to have made clear only so much.
I extended the length of the speech so much.
for where is there so great a goad as to kill one's mother?
so many things, herald, take from me.
then, at that time. Of past time
with changed accent τοτέ τοτέ [sometimes ... sometimes] (like ὁτὲ ὁτέ) now ... now
when the roar of the destructive snowstorm was at the gates, then I was lifted up with fear.
as much as they then honored Oedipus.
the Greeks then sang a solemn paean.
why then was the Darian so unharmed?
